title: Choose the layout for the chat-first study app
question: Three ways the tutor can open exercise panels in a chat. Same dark, minimal look in all three; only the layout differs. The moment shown: learning JavaScript Set.

options.label: Exercise stage
options.thesis: The current exercise takes the stage; the chat sits under it as a short thread.
options.viewport: Thin session sidebar. A large predict-the-output card fills the top of the centre column; the tutor's reply and the composer sit under it.
options.risk: Long explanations push the exercise up and out of view.

options.label: Lesson track
options.thesis: The lesson reads like one page of steps, as in Execute Program; the chat answers inline under each step.
options.viewport: Left rail lists the lesson steps and concept states. The centre column flows explanation, worked example, then the open exercise, with the tutor's reply under it.
options.risk: Feels more like a course than a conversation; free questions have less room.

options.label: Chat with side panel
options.thesis: A normal chat on the left; the tutor opens the exercise in a panel on the right, like t3code's side browser.
options.viewport: Sidebar, then the chat column with the tutor's explanation, then a wide panel with a mini editor (Vim keys) and test results.
options.risk: Three columns get tight on a laptop; the eye moves between chat and panel.
